text: A wall of tools on pegs, every one of them for cutting stone,
every one of them oiled, and a gap in the middle of the row
exactly the shape of the one that is out being used.
The kitchen counter, and a window over it looking at the mountain.
Every house on this street has that window. It is not a view,
it is a habit: you look up at the face before you go out to it.
Four chairs at a table laid for four, and a fifth chair against the wall
that has clearly not been at the table for some time.
A wireless set with a brass dial, tuned to the pit whistle band.
It has not carried a whistle in two years and nobody has retuned it.
